priorStories.headline: Ethiopian church says 60 killed in Oromia
priorStories.body:
The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church said attacks on Orthodox Christians in Oromia’s Arsi Zone killed 60 people and seriously injured more than 20. It attributed 14 deaths to an October 20 attack in Merti district and 46 to attacks in Shirka district on October 24.

Independent reports gave differing casualty estimates, and the perpetrators had not been publicly identified.

priorStories.headline: Jordan strikes Syria; main border crossing closes
priorStories.body:
Jordan carried out airstrikes in southern Syria against armed groups it linked to the October 23 attack on a Greek Orthodox funeral in Karak, Jordan. Jordan said militants were killed or wounded but did not identify the groups or disclose where it struck.

Syria said the operation was not coordinated with its government and killed seven civilians, including three children, in Daraa and Sweida. It then closed its main border crossing with Jordan.

priorStories.headline: New criminal case against Comey is unsealed
priorStories.body:
Newly unsealed court documents show that the Justice Department filed a criminal information against former FBI Director James Comey on October 5, alleging two felony counts related to disclosures of classified information in 2016.

The filing was made under seal and without a grand-jury indictment. Comey denies wrongdoing, and his lawyers asked the court to dismiss the case, arguing that it is legally invalid and was brought after the applicable limitations period.

candidates.summary: Polling stations opened across Israel for elections to all 120 seats in the Knesset. More than 7.3 million people were eligible to vote, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu facing a closely contested opposition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot. No single party was expected to win a majority, making coalition negotiations likely after ballots are counted.
candidates.title: Israelis vote in national election

candidates.summary: The Federal Trade Commission and 20 states sued Dollar General in federal court, alleging the retailer routinely charged customers more at checkout than prices displayed on shelves or in advertisements. The complaint says the company failed to correct the discrepancies despite extensive knowledge of them. Dollar General did not immediately comment to the Associated Press.
candidates.title: FTC and 20 states sue Dollar General over pricing

candidates.summary: A group of 21 Indian news publishers began a Supreme Court challenge to India’s privacy law. The publishers argue that requirements to obtain consent from people covered by journalists would amount to prior censorship, expose confidential sources and threaten newsroom operations.
candidates.title: Indian publishers challenge privacy law in Supreme Court

candidates.summary: Jordanian government spokesperson Mohammed al-Momani said Jordan’s overnight airstrikes in southern Syria killed more than 20 Islamic State militants. He said Jordan regretted civilian casualties reported by Syria, which said seven civilians, including three children and a woman, were killed. The strikes followed an October 23 attack on a funeral in Jordan.
candidates.title: Jordan says Syria strikes killed more than 20 Islamic State militants

candidates.summary: Polling ended in Israel’s Knesset election, with exit polls from the major television broadcasters indicating that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot secured the 61 seats needed for a majority. Likud was projected to be the largest party, but final results were still pending and coalition negotiations could take weeks.
candidates.title: Israeli exit polls indicate no clear election winner

candidates.summary: Heavy rains caused flooding and landslides across Haiti and the Dominican Republic. Haiti’s Civil Protection Agency reported at least four deaths, two people missing, more than 3,200 families affected and hundreds of homes destroyed. Dominican authorities said at least 30 communities were cut off and more than 100 homes flooded.
candidates.title: Flooding kills at least four in Haiti and cuts off communities on Hispaniola

candidates.summary: A federal grand jury in Washington declined to indict former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson after Justice Department prosecutors sought charges alleging that she lied to Congress about President Donald Trump’s actions surrounding the January 6, 2021, Capitol attack. The specific proposed charges were not publicly disclosed. Hutchinson has maintained that she stands by her testimony, and the Justice Department did not immediately comment.
candidates.title: Grand jury declines to indict Cassidy Hutchinson over January 6 testimony
